premises.text: Users—not sophisticated attackers—cause most breaches via password weakness
premises.evidence_span: over 86% of breaches today are caused by users and not by hackers

premises.text: Widely used enterprise access tools still leave a cloud-hosted single point of failure and adoption friction
premises.evidence_span: even if your company is using a single sign-on solution, an identity and access manager, or an enterprise password manager, the company still suffers from a fundamental flaw

premises.text: Phone biometric approval pushes credentials including 2FA into the browser and can remotely disconnect sessions
premises.evidence_span: put her fingerprint to authenticate. MyKey is going to push her username, her password, and even the additional SMS token

premises.text: Admin console provisions accounts, sets privilege and location/time/IP rules, and triggers background password changes without integrations
premises.evidence_span: You have to keep in mind that everything that I've shown you today requires no integration with service providers

premises.text: Monetization is freemium seats starting after five users for mid-size teams
premises.evidence_span: MyKey is free for the first five users and then starts at $5, $4.99 per additional user per month

value.text: Protect digital identity with simple, secure team access management

notes: Partition is need/product/pricing; justified because seat pricing can change without altering phone-push architecture, and breach/cloud-failure assumptions are market conditions independent of the product build. 40 customers excluded as traction.
